DigestMultibase.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.
DigestMultibase.title: DigestMultibase

OobKey.description: A starter key (`K_b`) or an approver lock key (`K_a`), as an Ed25519 `did:key` (`z6Mk…`) generated for this one request and used nowhere else. Ed25519 only: a service refuses any other key type with `auth/oob:keyUnsupported` before parsing beyond the multicodec prefix.
OobKey.title: OobKey

Origin.description: A web origin (`https://host[:port]`, no path, no trailing slash) — for `login`, the origin of the portal where the starter runs, which is the origin of the `serviceEndpoint` of the service's `SignInPortal` service in its DID document.
Origin.title: Origin

RequestId.description: The service-generated handle of one request: 16 to 32 bytes from a cryptographically secure random source, written as unpadded base64url (22 to 43 characters; 16 bytes, 22 characters, is RECOMMENDED). It is also the nonce of the exchange, so the family needs no separate challenge, and it is the `_id` of the trigger link (VTI-LNK-033). Compared as a string. It confers no authority on its holder.
RequestId.title: RequestId

SigningScope.description: The task families a `login` grant lets the starter key sign documents for, as the approving DID, for the session the grant arms (auth/oob/grant/0.2). Offered by the service in step 2, copied unchanged into the grant, and bounded further by the exclusions auth/oob/grant/0.2 states. Absent means the starter key signs nothing beyond the family's own tasks.
SigningScope.title: SigningScope

TaskFamily.description: A family of Trust Tasks, named by a slug prefix of whole segments (SPEC §6.1 grammar): `vtc/directory` names every task whose slug is `vtc/directory` or begins `vtc/directory/`, at any version. A prefix matches on segment boundaries only, so `vtc/dir` names nothing under `vtc/directory`.
TaskFamily.title: TaskFamily

schema.description: The member's decision on one out-of-band request, as an attestation: "let this starter key act as me at this origin until sessionEndsAt, having seen this context" — and, where the grant carries `signingScope`, "and sign documents of these task families as me, for that session" — or a decline. Issued by the DID that proved membership and signed by its VTA for `assertionMethod`, only after user verification. Never sent on its own, only carried inside auth/oob/respond/0.3. Closed: additionalProperties false and no `ext`. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

approverKey.description: The lock key `K_a`. MUST equal the issuer of the respond that carries this document.

contextDigest.description: SHA-256 multihash over the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form of the signed step 2 response document (the auth/oob/prove/0.3 response), proof included, written as multibase. Producers emit base58btc (`z…`). Binds the decision to exactly what the member was shown.

decision.description: The member's decision. A decline still names the context it declines, and needs no user verification.

origin.description: The portal origin from step 2, at which the session key may act.

sessionEndsAt.description: The latest instant the session key may act as the issuer, as an RFC 3339 date-time. The service ends the session at the earlier of this and its own session limit.

sessionKey.description: The starter key `K_b`, from step 2. On approve, the only key the grant lets act as the issuer.

signingScope.description: The task families the starter key may sign documents for as the issuer, for the session this grant arms — step 2's `signingScope`, copied unchanged. Absent: the grant delegates no signing. Whatever it names, a service never accepts the key for the exclusions auth/oob/grant/0.3 states (Conformance, consumer item 6), and never beyond the member's own standing.

schema.title: Auth — OOB Grant — payload
